Remarks on finite-time blow-up in a fully parabolic attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system via
reduction to the Keller–Segel system

Yutaro Chiyo, Tomomi Yokota** * Corresponding author.†† † Partially supported by Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (C), No. 21K03278.00 0 E-mail: ycnewssz@gmail.com, yokota@rs.tus.ac.jp

Department of Mathematics, Tokyo University of Science

1-3, Kagurazaka, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo 162-8601, Japan

August 24, 2026

  • Abstract. This paper deals with the fully parabolic attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system

    {ut=Δu−χ∇⋅(u∇v)+ξ∇⋅(u∇w),x∈Ω,t>0,vt=Δ​v−v+u,x∈Ω,t>0,wt=Δ​w−w+u,x∈Ω,t>0\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=\Delta u-\chi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v)+\xi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla w),&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\ v_{t}=\Delta v-v+u,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\ w_{t}=\Delta w-w+u,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0\end{cases}

    under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions and initial conditions, where Ω\Omega is an open ball in ℝn\mathbb{R}^{n} (n≥3n\geq 3), χ,ξ>0\chi,\xi>0 are constants. When w=0w=0, finite-time blow-up in the corresponding Keller–Segel system has already been obtained. However, finite-time blow-up in the above attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system has not yet been established except for the case n=3n=3. This paper provides an answer to this open problem by using a transformation which leads to a system presenting structural advantages respect to the original.

1 Introduction

In this paper we consider the fully parabolic attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system

{ut=Δu−χ∇⋅(u∇v)+ξ∇⋅(u∇w),x∈Ω,t>0,vt=Δ​v−v+u,x∈Ω,t>0,wt=Δ​w−w+u,x∈Ω,t>0,∇u⋅ν=∇v⋅ν=∇w⋅ν=0,x∈∂Ω,t>0,u(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x),w(x,0)=w0(x),x∈Ω,\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=\Delta u-\chi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v)+\xi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla w),&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.98753pt] v_{t}=\Delta v-v+u,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.98753pt] w_{t}=\Delta w-w+u,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[4.2679pt] \nabla u\cdot\nu=\nabla v\cdot\nu=\nabla w\cdot\nu=0,&x\in\partial\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.98753pt] u(x,0)=u_{0}(x),\ v(x,0)=v_{0}(x),\ w(x,0)=w_{0}(x),&x\in\Omega,\end{cases} (1.1)

where Ω≔B⁡(0,R)⊂ℝn\Omega\coloneqq B(0,R)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} (n≥3n\geq 3) is an open ball centered at the origin with radius R>0R>0; χ,ξ>0\chi,\xi>0 are constants; ν\nu is the outward normal vector to ∂Ω\partial\Omega. Moreover, the initial data u0,v0,w0u_{0},v_{0},w_{0} are supposed to be radially symmetric and positive functions which satisfy that

(u0,v0,w0)∈C0​(Ω¯)×W1,∞​(Ω)×W1,∞​(Ω).(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0})\in C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega).

In biology, the functions u,vu,v and ww represent the cell density, the concentration of attractive and repulsive chemical substances, respectively. The system (1.1) is one of variations of the chemotaxis system proposed by Keller and Segel [5] (see also Hillen–Painter [4]). The first equation in (1.1) describes the time evolution of the cell density in response to its own chemical attractants and repellents. Specifically, it implies that the cell movement is directed toward a higher concentration of the attractive signal and away from the repulsive signal.

On the other hand, in mathematics, it is important to consider whether a solution of the system (1.1) can blow up or not. In this paper we show finite-time blow-up of a solution to the system (1.1). The classical parabolic–elliptic Keller–Segel system and the parabolic–elliptic–elliptic attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system have been investigated in many literatures on chemotaxis systems (see e.g., Arumugam–Tyagi [1]). Before presenting the main result, we give an overview of known results about some problems related to (1.1).

We first focus on the parabolic–parabolic chemotaxis system

{ut=Δu−∇⋅(u∇v),vt=Δ​v−v+u.\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=\Delta u-\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v),\\[2.98753pt] v_{t}=\Delta v-v+u.\end{cases} (1.2)

The first result on unboundedness of solutions to (1.2) was established by Winkler [14]. After that, Winkler [15] succeeded in showing that a solution of (1.2) blows up in finite time under the condition that for all m>0m>0, A>0A>0, the initial data belongs to ℬ⁡(m,A)\mathcal{B}(m,A) which is the set of radially symmetric positive functions (φ,ψ)∈C0​(Ω¯)×W1,∞​(Ω)(\varphi,\psi)\in C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega) satisfying ∫Ωφ=m\int_{\Omega}\varphi=m, ‖ψ‖W1,2​(Ω)≤A\|\psi\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega)}\leq A and ℱ⁡(φ,ψ)≤−K⁡(m,A)\mathcal{F}(\varphi,\psi)\leq-K(m,A) with some K⁡(m,A)>0K(m,A)>0, where ℱ\mathcal{F} is the energy functional. Moreover, it was shown in [15] that ℬ⁡(m,A)\mathcal{B}(m,A) is dense in the space of all radially symmetric positive functions in C0​(Ω¯)×W1,∞​(Ω)C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega) with respect to the topology in Lp​(Ω)×W1,2​(Ω)L^{p}(\Omega)\times W^{1,2}(\Omega) for all p∈(1,2​nn+2)p\in(1,\frac{2n}{n+2}). Also, some related works which derive lower bound of blow-up time can be found in [2, 8, 9].

Secondly, we turn our eyes into the parabolic–elliptic chemotaxis system with signal-dependent sensitivity,

{ut=Δu−∇⋅(u∇v),0=Δ​v−v+u.\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=\Delta u-\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v),\\[2.98753pt] 0=\Delta v-v+u.\end{cases} (1.3)

As to this system, Nagai [10] derived that a radially symmetric solution blows up in finite time under some condition for the energy function and the moment of uu in two or more space dimensions. After that, in the two-dimensional setting, Nagai [11] proved that if ∫Ωu0​(x)​|x−x0|2​𝑑x\int_{\Omega}u_{0}(x)|x-x_{0}|^{2}\,dx for x0∈Ωx_{0}\in\Omega is sufficiently small and ∫Ωu0​(x)​𝑑x>8​πχ\int_{\Omega}u_{0}(x)\,dx>\frac{8\pi}{\chi} holds, then there exists a non-radial solution which blows up in finite time.

We now shift our attention to the parabolic–elliptic–elliptic version of the attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system

{ut=Δu−χ∇⋅(u∇v)+ξ∇⋅(u∇w),0=Δ​v+α​u−β​v,0=Δ​w+γ​u−δ​w,\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=\Delta u-\chi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v)+\xi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla w),\\[2.98753pt] 0=\Delta v+\alpha u-\beta v,\\[2.98753pt] 0=\Delta w+\gamma u-\delta w,\end{cases} (1.4)

where χ,ξ,α,β,γ,δ>0\chi,\xi,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta>0 are constants. Existence of a solution which blows up in finite time was studied by [7, 12, 16]. More precisely, in the two-dimensional setting, Tao and Wang [12] derived finite-time blow-up under the conditions that ∫Ωu0​(x)​|x−x0|2​𝑑x\int_{\Omega}u_{0}(x)|x-x_{0}|^{2}\,dx for x0∈Ωx_{0}\in\Omega is sufficiently small and that

  • (i) χ​α−ξ​γ>0\chi\alpha-\xi\gamma>0,  δ=β\delta=\beta and  ∫Ωu0​(x)​𝑑x>8​πχ​α−ξ​γ\int_{\Omega}u_{0}(x)\,dx>\frac{8\pi}{\chi\alpha-\xi\gamma}.

The idea in [12] is to reduce (1.4) to the form (1.3) by introducing the linear combination z≔χ​v−ξ​wz\coloneqq\chi v-\xi w. Also, in the two-dimensional setting, Li and Li [7] extended the above (i) to the following two conditions:

  • (ii) χ​α−ξ​γ>0\chi\alpha-\xi\gamma>0,  δ≥β\delta\geq\beta and  ∫Ωu0​(x)​𝑑x>8​πχ​α−ξ​γ\int_{\Omega}u_{0}(x)\,dx>\frac{8\pi}{\chi\alpha-\xi\gamma};

  • (iii) χ​α​δ−ξ​γ​β>0\chi\alpha\delta-\xi\gamma\beta>0,  δ<β\delta<\beta  and  ∫Ωu0​(x)​𝑑x>8​πχ​α​δ−ξ​γ​β\int_{\Omega}u_{0}(x)\,dx>\frac{8\pi}{\chi\alpha\delta-\xi\gamma\beta}.

After that, Yu, Guo and Zheng [16] improved the above (iii) by replacing χ​α​δ−ξ​γ​β\chi\alpha\delta-\xi\gamma\beta with χ​α−ξ​γ\chi\alpha-\xi\gamma in the first and third conditions in (iii) and filled the gap between the above (ii) and (iii); note that any relationship between δ\delta and β\beta is no longer necessary. On the other hand, in the two dimensional setting, Viglialoro [13] provided an explicit lower bound of blow-up time for the system (1.4).

For the fully parabolic attraction-repulsion system with positive parameters α,β,γ,δ\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta, i.e., the fully parabolic version of (1.4), Lankeit [6] succeeded in establishing existence of radially symmetric solutions blowing up at some finite time under the condition that χ​α−ξ​γ>0\chi\alpha-\xi\gamma>0 without any restriction on β,δ\beta,\delta in the three-dimensional setting.

In summary, finite-time blow-up has been shown for the parabolic–elliptic–elliptic attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system (1.4). However, finite-time blow-up in the fully parabolic system (1.1) has not been obtained yet except for the case n=3n=3.

The purpose of this paper is to give an answer to the above open problem, that is, to establish finite-time blow-up in the fully parabolic system (1.1). The strategy for proving finite-time blow-up is to apply the method in [15] to the system (1.1) via the linear combination of the solution components v,wv,w such that z≔χ​v−ξ​wz\coloneqq\chi v-\xi w. After this transformation, the analysis reduces to citing a well-known result from the literature, but a new information about blow-up in (1.1) is obtained.

2 Main results and their proofs

In this section we give two main theorems. The first one asserts finite-time blow-up in the system (1.1). The statement and proof read as follows.

Theorem 2.1.

Let Ω≔B⁡(0,R)⊂ℝn\Omega\coloneqq B(0,R)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} (n≥3)(n\geq 3) be an open ball centered at the origin with radius R>0R>0. Let m>0m>0, A>0A>0 and χ>ξ\chi>\xi. Then there exist constants T=T⁡(m,A)>0T=T(m,A)>0 and K=K⁡(m,A)>0K=K(m,A)>0 such that if (u0,v0,w0)(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0}) belongs to the set

𝒞(m,A):={(u0,v0,w0)∈C0(Ω¯)×W1,∞(Ω)×W1,∞(Ω)|\displaystyle\mathcal{C}(m,A):=\Big\{(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0})\in C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\,\Big|\,
u0​𝑎𝑛𝑑​χ​v0−ξ​w0​𝑎𝑟𝑒​𝑟𝑎𝑑𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑦​𝑠𝑦𝑚𝑚𝑒𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑐​𝑎𝑛𝑑​𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑖𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒​𝑖𝑛​Ω¯\displaystyle\hskip 71.13188ptu_{0}\ {\it and}\ \chi v_{0}-\xi w_{0}\ {\it are\ radially\ symmetric\ and\ positive\ in}\ {\overline{\Omega}}
𝑤𝑖𝑡ℎ∫Ωu0=m,∥χv0−ξw0∥W1,2​(Ω)≤A𝑎𝑛𝑑𝒢(u0,v0,w0)≤−K},\displaystyle\hskip 71.13188pt{\it with}\ \int_{\Omega}u_{0}=m,\ \|\chi v_{0}-\xi w_{0}\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega)}\leq A\ {\it and}\ \mathcal{G}(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0})\leq-K\Big\}, (2.1)

where 𝒢\mathcal{G} is the energy functional defined as

𝒢⁡(u0,v0,w0)\displaystyle\mathcal{G}(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0}) :=12​∫Ω|∇(χ​v0−ξ​w0)|2+12​∫Ω(χ​v0−ξ​w0)2\displaystyle:=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla(\chi v_{0}-\xi w_{0})|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}(\chi v_{0}-\xi w_{0})^{2}
−(χ−ξ)∫Ωu0(χv0−ξw0)+(χ−ξ)∫Ωu0lnu0,\displaystyle\qquad\quad-(\chi-\xi)\int_{\Omega}u_{0}(\chi v_{0}-\xi w_{0})+(\chi-\xi)\int_{\Omega}u_{0}\ln u_{0}, (2.2)

then the corresponding solution (u,v,w)(u,v,w) of the system (1.1) blows up before or at time TT.

Remark 2.1.

For n=3n=3, the above result is covered by [6, Theorem 1.1 with β=δ=1\beta=\delta=1].

Before proving the above theorem, we give the local solvability to clarify blow-up.

Lemma 2.2 ([12, Lemma 3.1]).

Let (u0,v0,w0)∈C0​(Ω¯)×W1,∞​(Ω)×W1,∞​(Ω)(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0})\in C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega). Then there exists Tmax∈(0,∞]T_{\rm max}\in(0,\infty] such that (1.1) possesses a unique classical solution (u,v,w)(u,v,w) such that

u,v,w∈C0​(Ω¯×[0,Tmax))∩C2,1​(Ω¯×(0,Tmax)),\displaystyle u,v,w\in C^{0}(\overline{\Omega}\times[0,T_{\rm max}))\cap C^{2,1}(\overline{\Omega}\times(0,T_{\rm max})),

and

𝑖𝑓​Tmax<∞,𝑡ℎ𝑒𝑛​limt↗Tmax‖u⁡(⋅,t)‖L∞​(Ω)=∞.\displaystyle{\it if}\ T_{\rm max}<\infty,\quad{\it then}\ \lim_{t\nearrow T_{\rm max}}\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}=\infty.

In particular, if u0≥0u_{0}\geq 0, then u⁡(⋅,t)≥0u(\cdot,t)\geq 0 for all t∈(0,Tmax)t\in(0,T_{\rm max}). Moreover, if u0,v0,w0u_{0},v_{0},w_{0} are radially symmetric in Ω¯{\overline{\Omega}}, then so are u,v,wu,v,w.

Proof of Theorem 2.1.

We introduce the linear combination of the variables (v,w)(v,w) such that z≔χ​v−ξ​wz\coloneqq\chi v-\xi w. Then the system (1.1) is rewritten as

{ut=Δu−∇⋅(u∇z),x∈Ω,t∈(0,Tmax),zt=Δ​z−z+(χ−ξ)​u,x∈Ω,t∈(0,Tmax),∇u⋅ν=∇z⋅ν=0,x∈∂Ω,t∈(0,Tmax),u(x,0)=u0(x),z(x,0)=z0(x),x∈Ω,\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=\Delta u-\nabla\cdot(u\nabla z),&x\in\Omega,\ t\in(0,T_{\rm max}),\\[2.98753pt] z_{t}=\Delta z-z+(\chi-\xi)u,&x\in\Omega,\ t\in(0,T_{\rm max}),\\[4.2679pt] \nabla u\cdot\nu=\nabla z\cdot\nu=0,&x\in\partial\Omega,\ t\in(0,T_{\rm max}),\\[2.98753pt] u(x,0)=u_{0}(x),\ z(x,0)=z_{0}(x),&x\in\Omega,\end{cases} (2.3)

where z0≔χ​v0−ξ​w0z_{0}\coloneqq\chi v_{0}-\xi w_{0} and χ>ξ\chi>\xi. We also define the energy functional for (2.3) as

ℱ⁡(u,z):=12​∫Ω|∇z|2+12​∫Ωz2−(χ−ξ)​∫Ωu​z+(χ−ξ)​∫Ωu​ln⁡u.\displaystyle\mathcal{F}(u,z):=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla z|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}z^{2}-(\chi-\xi)\int_{\Omega}uz+(\chi-\xi)\int_{\Omega}u\ln u.

Then the functional ℱ\mathcal{F} satisfies the energy inequality

dd​t​ℱ​(u⁡(⋅,t),z⁡(⋅,t))≤−𝒟⁡(u⁡(⋅,t),z⁡(⋅,t))for​all​t∈(0,Tmax),\displaystyle\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{F}(u(\cdot,t),z(\cdot,t))\leq-\mathcal{D}(u(\cdot,t),z(\cdot,t))\quad{\rm for\ all}\ t\in(0,T_{\rm max}), (2.4)

where 𝒟\mathcal{D} is the dissipation rate defined as

𝒟⁡(u,z)≔∫Ωzt2+(χ−ξ)​∫Ωu⋅|∇ln⁡u−∇z|2\displaystyle\mathcal{D}(u,z)\coloneqq\int_{\Omega}z_{t}^{2}+(\chi-\xi)\int_{\Omega}u\cdot\big|\nabla\ln u-\nabla z\big|^{2}

and Tmax∈(0,∞]T_{\rm max}\in(0,\infty] is the maximal existence time of the solution (u,z)(u,z) to the system (2.3). Indeed, in order to confirm (2.4), multiplying the second equation in (2.3) by ztz_{t}, we have

∫Ωzt2+dd​t​[12​∫Ω|∇z|2+12​∫Ωz2−(χ−ξ)​∫Ωu⁡(z−ln⁡u)]=(χ−ξ)​∫Ωut​(ln⁡u−z).\int_{\Omega}{z_{t}}^{2}+\frac{d}{dt}\Big[\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla z|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}z^{2}-(\chi-\xi)\int_{\Omega}u(z-\ln u)\Big]=(\chi-\xi)\int_{\Omega}u_{t}(\ln u-z).

This together with

∫Ωut(lnu−z)=−∫Ωu⋅|∇lnu−∇z|2\int_{\Omega}u_{t}(\ln u-z)=-\int_{\Omega}u\cdot\big|\nabla\ln u-\nabla z\big|^{2}

implies (2.4). Now we shall verify the conditions for blow-up in [15, Theorem 1.1] which asserts that for all m>0m>0 and A>0A>0 there exist T=T⁡(m,A)>0T=T(m,A)>0 and K=K⁡(m,A)>0K=K(m,A)>0 such that if (u0,z0)(u_{0},z_{0}) belongs to the set

ℬ(m,A):={(u0,z0)∈C0(Ω¯)×W1,∞(Ω)|\displaystyle\mathcal{B}(m,A):=\Big\{(u_{0},z_{0})\in C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\,\Big|\,
u0,z0​are​radially​symmetric​and​positive​in​Ω¯\displaystyle\hskip 71.13188ptu_{0},z_{0}\ {\rm are\ radially\ symmetric\ and\ positive\ in}\ {\overline{\Omega}}
with∫Ωu0=m,∥z0∥W1,2​(Ω)≤Aandℱ(u0,z0)≤−K},\displaystyle\hskip 71.13188pt{\rm with}\ \int_{\Omega}u_{0}=m,\ \|z_{0}\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega)}\leq A\ {\rm and}\ \mathcal{F}(u_{0},z_{0})\leq-K\Big\}, (2.5)

then the corresponding solution (u,z)(u,z) of (2.3) blows up before or at time TT, provided that χ−ξ=1\chi-\xi=1. Recalling that z=χ​v−ξ​wz=\chi v-\xi w, z0=χ​v0−ξ​w0z_{0}=\chi v_{0}-\xi w_{0} and

ℱ⁡(u0,z0)=𝒢⁡(u0,v0,w0),\mathcal{F}(u_{0},z_{0})=\mathcal{G}(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0}),

We next give and show the second main theorem, which guarantees that if the set 𝒞⁡(m,A)\mathcal{C}(m,A) defined in (2.1) equipped with a suitable topology, then it is dense in the space of radially symmetric positive functions.

Theorem 2.3.

Let Ω≔B⁡(0,R)⊂ℝn\Omega\coloneqq B(0,R)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} (n≥3)(n\geq 3) be an open ball centered at the origin with radius R>0R>0. Let p∈(1,2​nn+2)p\in(1,\frac{2n}{n+2}). Then for all m>0m>0, A>0A>0, the set 𝒞⁡(m,A){\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\mathcal{C}}(m,A) defined in (2.1) is dense in the space

Y:={(u,v,w)∈C0(Ω¯)×W1,∞(Ω)×W1,∞(Ω)|\displaystyle Y:=\Big\{(u,v,w)\in C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\,\Big|\,
u𝑎𝑛𝑑χv−ξw𝑎𝑟𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑑𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑦𝑠𝑦𝑚𝑚𝑒𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑖𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑖𝑛Ω¯}\displaystyle\hskip 38.41139ptu\ {\it and}\ \chi v-\xi w\ {\it are\ radially\ symmetric\ and\ positive\ in}\ {\overline{\Omega}}\Big\}

with respect to the topology in Lp​(Ω)×W1,2​(Ω)×W1,2​(Ω)L^{p}(\Omega)\times W^{1,2}(\Omega)\times W^{1,2}(\Omega), that is, for all (u0,v0,w0)∈𝒞⁡(m,A)(u_{0},v_{0},w_{0})\in\mathcal{C}(m,A) and all ε>0\varepsilon>0 there exists (u0​ε,v0​ε,w0​ε)∈Y(u_{0\varepsilon},v_{0\varepsilon},w_{0\varepsilon})\in Y such that

‖u0​ε−u0‖Lp​(Ω)+‖v0​ε−v0‖W1,2​(Ω)+‖w0​ε−w0‖W1,2​(Ω)<ε.\displaystyle\|u_{0\varepsilon}-u_{0}\|_{L^{p}(\Omega)}+\|v_{0\varepsilon}-v_{0}\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega)}+\|w_{0\varepsilon}-w_{0}\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega)}<\varepsilon.

In particular, the solution (uε,vε,wε)(u_{\varepsilon},v_{\varepsilon},w_{\varepsilon}) of the system (1.1) with initial data (uε,vε,wε)|t=0=(u0​ε,v0​ε,w0​ε)(u_{\varepsilon},v_{\varepsilon},w_{\varepsilon})|_{t=0}=(u_{0\varepsilon},v_{0\varepsilon},w_{0\varepsilon}) blows up in finite time.

Proof of Theorem 2.2.

Let n≥3n\geq 3, p∈(1,2​nn+2)p\in(1,\frac{2n}{n+2}), m>0m>0 and A>0A>0. Then we see from [15, Theorem 1.2] that the set ℬ⁡(m,A)\mathcal{B}(m,A) defined in (2.5) is dense in the space

X:={(u,z)∈C0(Ω¯)×W1,∞(Ω)|u,zareradiallysymmetricandpositiveinΩ¯},\displaystyle X:=\Big\{(u,z)\in C^{0}({\overline{\Omega}})\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\,\Big|\,u,z\ {\rm are\ radially\ symmetric\ and\ positive\ in}\ {\overline{\Omega}}\Big\},

and that for all (u0,z0)∈X(u_{0},z_{0})\in X and all ε>0\varepsilon>0 there exists (u0​ε,z0​ε)∈X(u_{0\varepsilon},z_{0\varepsilon})\in X such that the solution (uε,zε)(u_{\varepsilon},z_{\varepsilon}) of the system (2.3) with initial data (uε,zε)|t=0=(u0​ε,z0​ε)(u_{\varepsilon},z_{\varepsilon})|_{t=0}=(u_{0\varepsilon},z_{0\varepsilon}) blows up in finite time, which concludes the proof. ∎

Open problem.

Consider the fully parabolic attraction-repulsion chemotaxis system with positive parameters α,β,γ,δ\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta:

{ut=Δu−χ∇⋅(u∇v)+ξ∇⋅(u∇w),x∈Ω,t>0,vt=Δ​v−β​v+α​u,x∈Ω,t>0,wt=Δ​w−δ​w+γ​u,x∈Ω,t>0.\displaystyle\begin{cases}u_{t}=\Delta u-\chi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla v)+\xi\nabla\cdot(u\nabla w),&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.98753pt] v_{t}=\Delta v-\beta v+\alpha u,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0,\\[2.98753pt] w_{t}=\Delta w-\delta w+\gamma u,&x\in\Omega,\ t>0.\end{cases}

This cannot be reduced to the Keller–Segel system as in (2.3) via the transformation z=χ​u−ξ​wz=\chi u-\xi w in the case

β≠δ.\beta\neq\delta.

In this case, Lankeit [6] established finite-time blow-up in the three dimensional-setting. However, for n≥4n\geq 4, finite-time blow-up is left as an open problem.

Note.

After the completion of this paper, we confirmed that Fujie and Suzuki [3, Remark 1.5] derived Theorem 2.1 by the same transformation z=χ​u−ξ​wz=\chi u-\xi w.
